subject: Accounting
title: The Genius of Double Entry
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Genius of Double Entry usable.

hook.text: Luca Pacioli published the double-entry system in 1494. We still use it today—unchanged.

buildup.text: Double entry records every transaction twice—once as a debit and once as a credit.

discovery.text: This ensures the books always balance. If debits don't equal credits, something is wrong.

twist.text: The system is self-checking—errors reveal themselves because the equation breaks.

climax.text: Over 500 years later, every accounting system on Earth still follows Pacioli's elegant design.

punchline.text: 500 years old and still the foundation of all accounting.

quiz.question: Who published the double-entry bookkeeping system?

details.summary: Double-entry bookkeeping records every transaction in two equal and opposite entries, ensuring that the books always balance. Invented in Renaissance Italy, this system remains the foundation of all modern accounting worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Double-entry bookkeeping is arguably the most important invention in the history of commerce. It provides built-in error detection and a complete picture of how every transaction affects a business.
takeaways: Every transaction is recorded as both a debit and a credit of equal amounts
The system automatically detects errors because debits must always equal credits
Double-entry was first published by Luca Pacioli in 1494 and has endured for over 500 years

faq.question: What is double-entry bookkeeping?
faq.answer: Double-entry bookkeeping is a system where every financial transaction is recorded in at least two accounts—a debit in one and a credit in another—for equal amounts. This ensures the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) always stays balanced.

faq.question: Why is double-entry bookkeeping better than single-entry?
faq.answer: Double-entry provides built-in error detection (imbalanced entries signal mistakes), a complete picture of the business (both what you own and what you owe), and the ability to produce proper financial statements. Single-entry is just a list of cash transactions.
